My land is about 4 mu. I've farmed it the same way my whole life. Wheat in the fall, corn after the wheat. That's what we do here in Quzhou. My husband farmed this way, my father farmed this way. I'm 70 now, my body is not strong, but I know this land.

The wheat is already in the ground — I put it in last October, same as every year. I bought seeds from the supply store in town. I don't keep seeds myself anymore, those from the store grow better. I put compound fertilizer down before planting, then added urea when the plants came up to my knee in spring. I watered three times — once before the freeze, once when it started to joint, once more when it headed. My neighbor's son came with his sprayer to kill the aphids twice. That's how wheat is done.

For the corn, I'll plant it in June right after I harvest the wheat. Same 4 mu, same field. I buy the hybrid seeds — the ones everyone uses. I don't bother plowing, I just plant straight into the stubble, that's what my son told me to do and it saves my back. I put some fertilizer down at planting, then add urea once more when it gets tall. I'll water twice unless there's good rain. Maybe spray once if I see worms.

I don't grow vegetables or anything else. Too much trouble at my age, and I don't have anyone to help carry things to market.
